title: Spike: Capacitor wrap of the React app for iOS/iPadOS + Android
description: SWOT 10 recommendation: one React codebase covering iOS, iPadOS, Android, web, and mobile web via Capacitor is the pragmatic path for a content-first app, versus a React Native rewrite or a second native Kotlin app. Spike it: wrap the existing app, produce debug builds for both platforms, note gaps (localStorage persistence, external links, drawer UX), and write a go/no-go verdict.

title: Serve curriculum JSON from the server and automate the export
description: SWOT 10 weakness: scripts/export-curriculum.ts writes to a hardcoded sibling path and is a manual, easy-to-forget sync step, so clients can drift from src/data.ts. Add a GET /api/curriculum endpoint serving the same JSON, and/or a CI step that regenerates and verifies the export. Enables content updates to reach mobile clients without app-store releases (remote fetch with bundled fallback).
close_reason: Implemented, quality gate + runtime verification passed

title: Progress export/import as versioned JSON
description: SWOT 7 weakness: progress (completions, bookmarks, quiz scores) is device-locked in localStorage with no escape hatch; clearing browser data destroys it and multi-platform makes each surface an island. Add export-to-file and import-from-file of the progress blob, and add a schemaVersion field to the stored shape so future migrations are possible. This is the cheap bridge across web/iOS/Android and the migration path to optional accounts.
close_reason: Implemented, quality gate + runtime verification passed

title: Decide the fate of the native SwiftUI iOS app
description: SWOT 10 threat: maintaining separate native UIs per platform for a curated-content app is unsustainable. Once the Capacitor spike verdict lands, decide whether the sibling ai-engineer-learning-guide-ios SwiftUI app is retired, demoted to maintenance mode, or kept as the flagship iOS experience, and record the decision.

title: Hosted LLM backend story for mobile clients
description: SWOT 10 weakness: mobile apps cannot assume a local Ollama at localhost:11434, so Study Buddy needs a hosted OpenAI-compatible backend (the Ollama Cloud path in server.ts already exists). Document and wire the deployment story for mobile builds: which base URL the app talks to, operator cost controls, and confirm the existing rate limiting is adequate.

title: Enforce at-most-one start-here resource per topic
description: SWOT 3 weakness: the 'at most one start-here per topic' rule is enforced by convention only. Add a validation check (in scripts/export-curriculum.ts or a lint step run by npm run lint) that fails when a topic has more than one start-here resource, so the invariant is machine-checked.

title: Fix Study Buddy interview retry after a failed turn
description: Known bug from docs/code-analysis.md: in StudyBuddy.tsx the error-retry button calls handleSendMessage() with an empty input, so a failed interview turn cannot actually be retried. Preserve the last user message and resend it on retry.

title: LLM backend health check and friendly unavailable-state UX
description: SWOT 6 weakness: if Ollama is not running (or the cloud key is bad), Study Buddy features fail at request time with a generic 500. Add a health check (e.g. GET /api/ai/health pinging the configured base URL) and have the client show an actionable message (start Ollama / check key) instead of a generic error.

title: Automated periodic link checker over curriculum resources
description: SWOT 1 weakness/threat: the 122-resource link audit was a point-in-time snapshot (2026-07-11) and link rot is inevitable; re-verification is manual. Add a scheduled CI job (or npm script) that checks liveness/redirects for every resource URL in src/data.ts and files a report of dead or moved links. Include the Depth Zero day-one exercise dependencies in the check, since a broken first-run experience is the worst failure mode.

title: Mobile-web layout audit and polish
description: SWOT 8/10: the web UI has responsive breakpoints but the filter bar (5 buttons + search) is desktop-shaped and cramped at phone widths, and the Study Buddy drawer needs checking at small sizes. Audit the full UI at phone widths and fix tap targets, wrapping, and drawer behavior.

title: Capstone starter scaffolding and shareable artifact
description: SWOT 4 weakness: the capstone thread exists only as copy, with no starter repo, checkpoints, or way to show off a finished capstone. Create a starter template repo plus per-step checkpoint descriptions, and a simple share/export artifact (e.g. a completion summary) learners can link publicly. Keep the free tier substantive so it does not read as an ad for premium.

title: Replace home-grown markdown renderer with react-markdown
description: SWOT 5 weakness (also flagged in docs/code-analysis.md): StudyBuddy.tsx uses a home-grown markdown renderer, acceptable for a prototype but a growing liability as LLM output variety increases. Swap it for react-markdown (or similar) with code-block highlighting parity.

title: Stable resource IDs; key bookmarks by ID instead of URL
description: SWOT 8 weakness: bookmarks are keyed by resource URL, so fixing a URL during a link audit silently breaks existing bookmarks. Add stable id fields to resources in src/data.ts, key bookmarks by id, and migrate existing URL-keyed bookmarks (relies on the progress schemaVersion field from the progress export/import work).

title: CONTRIBUTING.md with resource audit checklist
description: SWOT 1 opportunity: community contributions via PRs against src/data.ts could scale curation, but only with a quality bar. Write a CONTRIBUTING.md that documents the resource audit checklist (liveness, free access, currency, paywall flagging, one start-here per topic) so external PRs meet the same standard as the original audit.

title: Stream Study Buddy explain and interview responses
description: SWOT 5 weakness: no streaming, so long explanations render only when complete and feel slow on weaker local hardware. Stream tokens from the /api/ai/explain and /api/ai/interview endpoints (SSE or chunked) and render incrementally in StudyBuddy.tsx.

title: Content changelog so returning learners see what changed
description: SWOT 1 weakness: there is no versioning or changelog for curriculum content, so learners cannot see what changed since their last visit and the '2026 Edition' label dates itself. Add a lightweight content changelog (date + change entries, surfaced in the UI or README) updated whenever data.ts changes.

title: Interactive Depth Zero on-ramp checklist
description: SWOT 2 weakness/opportunity: the Depth Zero on-ramp is one static step with no feedback loop confirming the learner shipped something. Turn it into an interactive in-app checklist (ship your first LLM call) with completion persisted alongside existing progress, optionally wired to the Study Buddy for help when stuck.

value: User preference: delegate execution work to smaller models (haiku for mechanical tasks, sonnet for moderate coding); reserve the top model for planning, review, and judgment-heavy work.
